177	- The [registry](https://opentelemetry.io/ecosystem/registry/) already has tools for searching for components, and displaying bits of information about them, but its insufficient. More than anything else, the registry is an index of links, requiring the user to follow the link and find installation / configuration / telemetry schema details in the linked website / repository. 3	# Meeting Note: OpenTelemetry Go SIG — 2025-11-03
4	
5	**Canonical URL**: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/6648#issuecomment-3479655348  
6	**Author**: pellared

16	- Bryan Boreham
17	- Damien Mathieu
18	- Robert Pająk
19	- David Ashpole
20	- Mike Blum
21	
22	## Transcript
23	
24	### Monitoring bugs reported by OSS-Fuzz
25	- David proposed enabling automatic filing of OSS-Fuzz findings as GitHub issues to track and triage them in-repo.
26	- Robert noted OSS-Fuzz runs in Google CI; access and notifications currently limited. Some maintainers may need to be added as contacts.
27	- Tyler and David highlighted that OSS-Fuzz does not file public issues by default due to potential security sensitivity of fuzz findings.
28	- Consensus:
29	  - Start by setting up a maintainers mailing list for OSS-Fuzz notifications (via GC) and trial monitoring for a few months.
30	  - Avoid enabling public GitHub issue filing for now; reassess after triage/verification workflows are in place.
31	  - Robert can manually recreate older issues if needed.
32	- Bryan shared Prometheus project’s recent discussion comparing OSS-Fuzz with Go’s built-in fuzzing; Robert emphasized OSS-Fuzz’s continuous background fuzzing as a benefit.
33	
34	References:
35	- [Monitoring bugs reported by OSS Fuzz #7549](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/7549)
36	
37	### Stabilization of otelgrpc
38	- Community request to stabilize otelgrpc noted by Tyler.
39	- Blockers:
40	  - Stabilization of RPC semantic conventions (semconv) must come first.
41	  - Audit of the current otelgrpc API to remove cruft and confirm stability.
42	- Damien clarified that stabilization does not imply restoring the old interceptor—it should remain removed.
43	- David is willing to drive module stability once semconv stabilizes; however, gRPC engagement has been sporadic and driven by their internal roadmap.
44	- Strategy discussion:
45	  - OTel could continue owning and maintaining a gRPC instrumentation package, with the option to deprecate later if gRPC ships native instrumentation aligned with semconv.
46	  - Seek more engagement from gRPC; attempt in-person conversations at KubeCon if possible. David will sync with Josh on outreach.
47	- Conclusion: Not likely to stabilize this year; set a goal to finalize a strategy next year once semconv progress is clearer.
48	
49	References:
50	- [Stabilization of otelgrpc](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-contrib/issues/8078)?
51	  - Related: [https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/8265](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/8265)  
52	  - We need the semconv to stabilize  
53	  - There needs to be involvement from gRPC to progress this  
54	  - [David] Update: I’m told that the SIG is active and is working towards stabilization. Not sure if gRPC is involved.  
55	
56	### Stabilization of otelhttp
57	- Damien proposed starting an API audit for otelhttp to move towards stabilization.
58	- A known bug (issue #7254) may be the only blocker; it’s a behavioral change around how errors are marked (events vs attributes) and interacts with semconv/spec wording.
59	- Agreement:
60	  - Begin the API review.
61	  - Robert will take ownership of #7254 and draft a document clarifying interpretation and proposed resolution.
62	  - The existence of bugs does not inherently block stabilization; they can be fixed post-stabilization if changes are non-breaking or properly versioned.
63	
64	References:
65	- Blocker (only one I think): [https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-contrib/issues/7254](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-contrib/issues/7254)  
66	
67	### OTel Explorer Go docs
68	- Mike outlined a project to revamp the OTEL registry/explorer with a schema that documents spans/metrics emitted by instrumentations, aiming to render via Hugo and enable static analysis across Go SDKs and contrib modules.
69	- Tyler’s feedback:
70	  - Strong requirement: align schema with semantic conventions and ensure it’s compatible with Weaver (to enable validation and transformations across versions).
71	  - Consider providing a JSON Schema (or CUE) for validation and potentially linking to existing semconv definitions to keep the spec concise.
72	  - Scope can include eBPF/auto-instrumentation; representation should still fit the schema as long as it maps to OTEL signals.
73	- Mike will iterate on the schema, explore Weaver integration, and coordinate with SIGs as needed.
74	
75	References:
76	  - Context: [https://github.com/open-telemetry/community/pull/3000](https://github.com/open-telemetry/community/pull/3000)  
77	  - Meeting notes: [Ecosystem Explorer Project](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1QBpFmSR54fGus8q6RraUj0-mEjSoX7S7fdlgsvxZsuk/edit?usp=sharing)  
78	  - [https://github.com/mikeblum/otel-explorer-go-docs/blob/3797539be4f5a760e99586c0de72496019f5e6b0/instrumentation-list.yaml](https://github.com/mikeblum/otel-explorer-go-docs/blob/3797539be4f5a760e99586c0de72496019f5e6b0/instrumentation-list.yaml)  
79	
80	### SIG Security: release signing
81	- Robert proposed enabling GitHub “signature releases” in addition to existing tag signing and GPG signatures of source archives.
82	- Key points:
83	  - GitHub’s source tarball/zip is generated at download time; signing artifacts strengthens trust and mitigates changes over time.
84	  - Double-signing is acceptable and beneficial for OSS Scorecard/compliance.
85	  - Constraint: Artifacts must be uploaded at release time; cannot regenerate later.
86	- Decision: Proceed with enabling signature releases; update release documentation and ensure process discipline.
87	
88	References:
89	- [https://github.com/open-telemetry/sig-security/issues/164](https://github.com/open-telemetry/sig-security/issues/164)  
90

93	- Go SIG will meet at the booth (Tuesday morning, local time; check published schedule).
94	- Plan to cancel the Zoom SIG meeting during KubeCon week; reminder will be sent next week.

99	  - Work with GC to set up a maintainers mailing list for OSS-Fuzz notifications and ensure appropriate access for Go SIG maintainers.
100	  - Consider manual recreation of older OSS-Fuzz issues if needed; revisit auto GitHub issue filing after triage process matures.
101	  - Take ownership of otelhttp issue [#7254](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-contrib/issues/7254); draft a document clarifying error marking approach and semconv alignment.
102	  - Enable GitHub signature releases for OTel Go; update releasing docs; ensure artifacts are uploaded at release time and signatures published. Reference: [sig-security #164](https://github.com/open-telemetry/sig-security/issues/164).
103	- Damien:

content.text:
## Answer

**No — the corpus does not show an Ecosystem Explorer implementation being delivered.** Only the *proposal* is established as complete; the implementation/product delivery is explicitly recorded as not established.

### What is established

**The proposal merged, and that is all it did.**
- `open-telemetry/community#3000`, "Project Proposal: Ecosystem Explorer" (author `jaydeluca`), was opened 2025-09-19 and **merged/closed by `trask` on 2025-12-01T19:04:18Z**. It changed **+251 / -0 across 2 files** — a proposal document (`projects/ecosystem-explorer.md`, renamed from `projects/instrumentation-documentation.md`), not code.
  `/Users/markpyzhov/VSCodeProjects/corpuses-arms/c2/opentelemetry/pulls/community-3000.md`
- The proposal itself notes it was gated on staffing: it was to be used "to socialize the effort in hopes of finding people interested in participating" (same file, Description).

**The Work State is explicit that delivery did not follow.**
- `T006` (mapped to `community#3000`) is checked complete, but scoped strictly to the **project proposal PR**: "Ecosystem Explorer **project proposal** PR. Merged."
- Done / Evidence: "merged/closed 2025-12-01 `(SRC-PR-02)`. **Explorer product delivery not established.**"
- Next Update Needed lists, as still outstanding: "**Explorer implementation beyond the proposal PR.**"
  `/Users/markpyzhov/VSCodeProjects/corpuses-arms/c2/work-states/WS-05-contrib.md` (Status: in_progress, Last Updated 2026-03-08)
- The registry index concurs: `community#3000` → "proposal merged; **Explorer delivery not established**."
  `/Users/markpyzhov/VSCodeProjects/corpuses-arms/c2/work-states/index.md`

### Post-merge activity that exists (but is not delivery)

- Pre-merge, the Go SIG meeting of 2025-10-30 discussed "OTel Explorer Go docs": Mike Blum outlined revamping the registry/explorer with a schema for spans/metrics emitted by instrumentations, rendered via Hugo. Tyler Yahn set requirements — align the schema with semantic conventions, ensure **Weaver compatibility**, and provide a **JSON Schema (or CUE) for validation**. Mike's action item was to *iterate on the schema*, i.e. still design-stage work.
  `/Users/markpyzhov/VSCodeProjects/corpuses-arms/c2/opentelemetry/meeting-notes/entry-3479655348.md`
- After the merge, PR #3000's timeline shows only **cross-references** from other items — `community#3175` (2025-12-02), `community#3128` (2025-12-04), `community#3230` (2026-01-20), and `community#3435` (2026-05-13). None of these referenced items are present in this package, so their content, state, and whether any constitutes implementation cannot be determined from the available evidence.
  `/Users/markpyzhov/VSCodeProjects/corpuses-arms/c2/opentelemetry/pulls/community-3000.md`

### Bottom line

The premise that an implementation was delivered is not supported. What merged on 2025-12-01 was a governance/proposal document; the only implementation-adjacent artifact anywhere in the package is a pre-proposal POC referenced in the PR description (`jaydeluca.github.io/instrumentation-explorer/`) and Mike Blum's prototype `instrumentation-list.yaml` schema, both predating the merge. The package's data was collected 2026-07-14 and the governing Work State was last updated 2026-03-08, and as of that state the Explorer implementation remained an open item.
